The glyfp package provides a separate function for each structural fingerprint
or pretrained glycan representation. Each returns a list of named vectors,
one per input glycan, and exposes only options relevant to its method. Inputs can
be glyrepr structure vectors or text in formats supported by glyparse.

## Choose a method

| Function | Coordinates | Source of features |
|---|---|---|
| `fp_motif_binary()` | Presence/absence; 3,173 dimensions by default | Fixed glydb motif dictionary |
| `fp_motif_count()` | Overlapping occurrences; same dimensions | Same fixed dictionary |
| `fp_sweetnet()` | 128 pretrained features | SweetNet v2 by default; legacy v1 also supported |
| `fp_glycangt()` | 768 pretrained graph Transformer features | Large mask-35 model; local checkpoint required |
| `fp_gifflar()` | 384 pretrained molecular graph features | Species model; local checkpoint required |

### Migrating existing calls

The former `glycan_fingerprint()` interface has been replaced by these functions.
For example, replace `glycan_fingerprint(x, "substructure_count", max_size = 2)`
with `fp_motif_count(x, max_size = 2)`, and `glycan_fingerprint(x, "sweetnet")`
with `fp_sweetnet(x)`. Default calls `glycan_fingerprint(x)` become
`fp_motif_binary(x)`. The resulting vectors and defaults are unchanged.

`max_size` and `unknown` belong to the two motif functions. Only `fp_sweetnet()`
accepts `cache_dir` and `download`. For GlycanGT and GIFFLAR, pass the required
local `checkpoint` and omit any former `download = FALSE` argument. All five
functions accept `na_action`; embedding functions always reject unknown tokens.

Every method processes complete structures. Specify concrete residues, all
linkage positions and anomers, substituent positions, and the reducing-end
alpha/beta state. For example, `Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-` is complete;
`Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc` leaves the reducing-end state unknown and is rejected.
Validation inspects normalized glyrepr graph fields for text and object inputs.
Empty substituent fields mean no modification, not unknown chemistry.
Alditols and unresolved floating components/substituents are outside scope.
Missing inputs (`NA`) are supported separately from uncertain structures.

## Substructure fingerprints

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
```

```{r}
library(glyfp)
a <- c("Galb3Galb3Galb-", "Galb-")
b <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
fp_a <- fp_motif_count(a)
fp_b <- fp_motif_count(b)
lengths(fp_a)
stopifnot(identical(c(fp_a, fp_b),
                   fp_motif_count(c(a, b))))
```

The same glycan receives the same coordinates alone, in another batch, or in
another order. Other inputs never redefine its dictionary. Text parsing is
delegated to glyparse; equivalent objects yield the same values.

```{r}
objects <- glyparse::auto_parse(a)
stopifnot(identical(fp_motif_count(objects), fp_a))
fp_a[[1]][c("Gal(b1-", "Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-")]
```

Overlap counts: a Gal-Gal motif occurs twice in the three-Gal chain. Counts use
glymotif's strict substructure matching, including linkage and substituent labels.
Symmetric mappings of the same residue set count once. Binary fingerprints are
`as.integer(count > 0)`. Reducing-end alpha/beta information is retained:

```{r}
ends <- fp_motif_binary(c("Gal(a1-", "Gal(b1-"))
lapply(ends, function(x) x[c("Gal(a1-", "Gal(b1-")])
```

### Dictionary source and coverage

The built-in dictionary is **`glydb-2.12.1-complete-v1`**. It uses glydb
0.7.2.9000 at commit `cafa287eac546a9899977a9e8c777af77cfd2ac3`, whose structures
come from [GlyGen reviewed release 2.12.1](https://data.glygen.org/ln2data/releases/data/v-2.12.1/reviewed/).
Of 49,728 parsed source records, 8,416 accessions pass complete-structure checks,
representing 8,211 unique structures. The other 41,312 records are excluded.
Exclusion reasons overlap: 31,654 uncertain reducing ends; 23,836 uncertain
linkages; 6,218 floating parts; 4,443 alditols; 2,681 nonconcrete residues;
637 uncertain substituents; and 27 floating substituents. Before this step,
glydb's preparation excluded 10,266 parsing failures from 59,994 source records.
Coverage therefore reflects that parser and source snapshot.

Connected motifs include branches and all sizes up to `max_size`, not just
fragments of exactly that size. The dictionary contains 24,124 motifs with
exact-size counts of 134, 906, 2,133, 3,110, 4,355, 5,849 and 7,637 for sizes
1–7. The default `max_size = 3` selects 3,173 features and retains mono- and
disaccharide information. Features are canonical strings sorted by UTF-8 bytes;
no hashing or folding is used. Higher sizes can require more enumeration work.

The installed `extdata/motif-dictionary-metadata.R` records source and dictionary
SHA-256 hashes, included-accession hash, exclusions and generator versions.
The source repository's `data-raw/build-motif-dictionary.R` reproduces the
resource from the pinned glydb artifact. GlyGen database sets use
[CC BY 4.0](https://www.glygen.org/license/); attribution and changes are recorded
in the installed `COPYRIGHTS` file. The glydb package code is MIT licensed.

The connected-fragment design is informed by
[*Glycan Fingerprints: Calculating Diversity in Glycan Libraries* (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1021/cb300003z)
and its [official supporting information](https://acs.figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/Glycan_Fingerprints_Calculating_Diversity_in_Glycan_Libraries/2521345).
That paper uses 1–7-residue connected subtrees and hashed/folded binary strings;
it does not supply this fixed explicit dictionary. glyfp does not reproduce its
dataset-dependent occupancy correction or modified Tanimoto score.

An unseen motif never adds coordinates. `unknown = "ignore"` counts only known
motifs; `"warn"` also warns and `"error"` rejects unseen motifs. This policy
controls dictionary coverage, not uncertain input: unknown structural fields
are always rejected. Different `max_size` values or dictionary versions define
different coordinate sets. Save the method, options and glyfp version alongside
results; recompute compared fingerprints after a dictionary change.

```{r}
stopifnot(length(fp_motif_binary(character())) == 0L)
missing <- fp_motif_binary(NA_character_)[[1]]
stopifnot(length(missing) == 3173L, all(is.na(missing)))
path <- tempfile(fileext=".rds")
saveRDS(fp_a, path)
stopifnot(identical(readRDS(path), fp_a))
unlink(path)
```

## Pretrained embeddings

All embedding methods use optional R torch on the CPU. Binary/count methods do
not load torch or require a model runtime. Install the optional dependencies and
runtime explicitly once; glyfp never installs them automatically:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("torch", "digest", "zip"))
torch::install_torch()
```

Input validation still requires a known reducing-end alpha/beta state. The
pretrained models do not encode that state, so **only after validation** glyfp
projects it out at the normal reducing carbon. Consequently, glycans differing
only in reducing-end alpha/beta have identical embeddings but distinct motif
fingerprints where the corresponding motifs are in the dictionary. Other
reducing-end positions or unsupported chemistry produce errors. No other
unknown structure is accepted or silently completed.

Under the same model, checkpoint, preprocessing and runtime settings, duplicate
glycans, input order and batch size do not affect coordinates. CPU evaluation
uses float32, frozen normalization, no dropout or gradients, and one graph per
forward pass. Save the method, checkpoint identity and package/runtime versions
with the resulting vectors. Different model versions define different spaces,
even when lengths and coordinate names match. Cross-platform comparisons should
allow floating-point tolerance; reference tests bound every coordinate's absolute
error by `1e-5`. All-NA inputs retain the model's full coordinate set.

### SweetNet

[SweetNet (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2021.109251) is a graph neural
network over residues and linkages. `fp_sweetnet()` defaults to v2 and
returns 128 coordinates from `bn2(lin2(...))`, before final activation, dropout
and classification.

**No environment variable or manual download is required for SweetNet.** On first
use, glyfp downloads the pinned official checkpoint, verifies SHA-256 and saves
it in `tools::R_user_dir("glyfp", "cache")`. Subsequent calls verify and reuse it.

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Maintainer switch: normal documentation builds do not download model weights.
run_sweetnet <- identical(Sys.getenv("GLYFP_RUN_MODEL_EXAMPLES"), "true")
```

```{r, eval=run_sweetnet}
a <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", "GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
fp <- fp_sweetnet(a)
lengths(fp)
offline <- fp_sweetnet(a, download = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(fp, offline))
legacy <- fp_sweetnet(a, checkpoint = "sweetnet-v1")
```

| Checkpoint | Model |
|---|---|
| `"sweetnet-v2"` (default; about 3.82 MB) | Residual graph layers with BatchNorm; mean and max pooling |
| `"sweetnet-v1"` | Legacy glycowork 1.9.0 species model; three graph layers and mean pooling |
| Local `.pt` path | Either supported official artifact, identified by its hash |

Both versions return 128 coordinates, but their values must not be mixed.
The v2 default follows the current upstream model, not a claim of better accuracy
for every task. `cache_dir` changes the cache location; `download = FALSE`
prevents network access and errors on an offline cache miss. A local file is
never replaced or copied to a persistent cache:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fp <- fp_sweetnet(a,
  checkpoint = "/path/to/glycowork_sweetnet_species_v2.pt", download = FALSE)
```

Downloads use a temporary file, SHA-256 validation and atomic rename. Corrupt
cache entries produce an error naming the file; remove that entry to permit a
fresh download or supply a verified local file. Failed downloads leave no
partial checkpoint to be mistaken for valid weights. Loading glyfp or using
motif methods makes no network request. Original checkpoint files are never
modified; legacy CUDA tags are relocated in a temporary CPU copy.

Supported MIT-licensed official artifacts:

- [SweetNet v2](https://huggingface.co/DBojar/glycowork_models/blob/52187c054b9c988ddb2a5a5af9ee64b51004fd1e/glycowork_sweetnet_species_v2.pt),
  SHA-256 `bc3d901e4284554c1a245b8e6b7e291a5631c8932ca9c27eb8668b6d4424a146`.
- [Legacy SweetNet](https://huggingface.co/DBojar/glycowork_models/blob/0a3981df888532e52b4c2d910bfb56b5a45ad955/glycowork_sweetnet_species.pt),
  SHA-256 `4ee19fc0593db0562c16585b556050694144816754750ebfe1876ed21ba0f4be`.

Every residue/substituent/linkage token must be in the fixed vocabulary.
Embedding functions always reject unknown tokens; no untrained token is used.
The configurable `unknown` argument belongs only to motif functions.

### GlycanGT

[GlycanGT](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btag147) uses residue and linkage
tokens in a graph Transformer. The supported large model trained with 35%
node-and-edge masking returns its final 768-dimensional graph token.

**Download its checkpoint yourself and supply a local path. glyfp never downloads
GlycanGT weights.** Obtain access under the conditions of the
[official model repository](https://huggingface.co/Akikitani295/GlycanGT), then
download `outputs/mask_35/pretrained_tokengt_large_multitask_mask_35_final.pt`
(about 367 MB). The upstream project declares Apache-2.0; model access has a
separate step. Do not put account credentials into R code.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fp <- fp_glycangt(
  c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", "Man(a1-3)[Man(a1-6)]Man(a1-"),
  checkpoint = "/path/to/pretrained_tokengt_large_multitask_mask_35_final.pt")
lengths(fp) # 768 768
```

The supported Hugging Face revision is
`7c9f4a19b366ca48ed03995a0ad47fa1e745f24c`, SHA-256
`d490d18795ee6d4746b9b4abd0a5c733d8f7e4261998d050c1b741b65e530a54`.
Code follows [the fixed official implementation](https://github.com/matsui-lab/GlycanGT/tree/96611518c971deb89215ca163deaf9de3a59fa32).
Omitting the local checkpoint or supplying a URL produces an error.
`fp_glycangt()` has no `download` or `cache_dir` argument.
Every call hashes the original file, even with tensors cached in memory. CUDA
tags are relocated in a temporary CPU copy without changing the original file.

The official model generates orthogonal random node identifiers even in
`eval()`. glyfp fixes one draw per canonical **projected** glycan: master seed
1729 plus a SHA-256-derived graph seed, the original single-graph Gaussian QR
construction, and padding/truncation to width 64. Reducing-end alpha/beta is
omitted before canonicalization and seed construction. Caller R and CPU torch
RNG states are preserved. Upstream multi-graph batches use their maximum node
count and may give different identifiers and outputs. This deterministic policy
is not a claim to reproduce the paper's downstream benchmark performance.

At least two residues and tokens in the fixed vocabulary are required; the
upstream edge-triple pipeline does not retain edge-free graphs. Real pretrained
reference comparisons cover 12 glycans and every coordinate under the same
single-graph identifier policy, not the upstream stochastic multi-graph policy.

### GIFFLAR

[GIFFLAR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13467) combines atoms, bonds and residues through
heterogeneous message passing. The R implementation follows the pinned
[glycowork network and graph builder](https://github.com/BojarLab/glycowork/tree/199efdde6bc137dbbcd900f84f927fdbbca52eae).
It concatenates three independent means into 384 coordinates, not the 1,076
classification scores. No Python, RDKit or GlyLES runtime is needed.

Download `glycowork_gifflar_species.pt` (about 7.8 MB) from the
[official fixed revision](https://huggingface.co/DBojar/glycowork_models/tree/52187c054b9c988ddb2a5a5af9ee64b51004fd1e).
The code and model card declare MIT licensing. glyfp requires a local file and
never downloads GIFFLAR weights. SHA-256:
`0dab7c3b61aad95dab37d4974da4b57b3fd985128dc09ad5da846e82adb9519d`.
Every call verifies it, including when tensors are already cached in memory.
`fp_gifflar()` has no `cache_dir` or `download` argument.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fp <- fp_gifflar(c("GlcNAc(b1-", "Gal6S(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_),
  checkpoint = "/path/to/glycowork_gifflar_species.pt")
lengths(fp) # 384 384 384
```

The native graph builder supports 27 fixed residue labels:

| Group | Residues |
|:--|:--|
| Unmodified | Glc, Gal, Man, Fuc, Xyl, Rha, Rib, Ara |
| Amino and N-acetyl | GlcN, GalN, GlcNAc, GalNAc, ManNAc |
| Uronic and sialic acids | GlcA, GalA, IdoA, Neu5Ac, Neu5Gc, Kdn |
| Positioned sulfates | Gal6S, GlcNAc6S, GlcNAc3S, GalNAc4S, GalNAc6S, IdoA2S |
| Positioned phosphates | Glc6P, Man6P |

Monosaccharides are supported. Other templates, anomeric-to-anomeric bonds and
attachments that would move or extend a modification are rejected. For example,
a child attached at position 2 of GlcN or position 6 of Glc6P is unsupported.
There is no approximate molecular fallback. For short ambiguous text, use an
explicit complete serialization such as `Ara(a1-` or an ecosystem parser.

The molecular graph retains official atom/chirality features, bond ownership,
ring relations and both directions of linkage features. Bond order and charge
are not separate input features in the official network. Atom, bond and residue
means are pooled separately. No random identifiers are used. Graphs and real
pretrained predictions have been checked against pinned upstream code on 86
structures covering every supported template and both linkage anomers.

## Validation

Normal tests do not require network access. Small untrained networks validate
ported operators independently of checkpoint access; they are not pretrained
models. Real integration tests additionally use locally supplied files through
developer-only variables `GLYFP_TEST_CHECKPOINT`, `GLYFP_TEST_V2_CHECKPOINT`,
`GLYFP_TEST_GLYCANGT_CHECKPOINT` and `GLYFP_TEST_GIFFLAR_CHECKPOINT`. These tests
cover numerical references, explicit complete input followed by the documented
root projection, independent batches, duplicates, object/text equivalence,
missingness, RNG preservation and unchanged original weight files.
